paper_title: The eVALuate study: two parallel randomised trials, one comparing laparoscopic with abdominal hysterectomy, the other comparing laparoscopic with vaginal hysterectomy
design_rationale: This comprises two parallel randomized trials in which treatment allocation used telephone access to a centrally held computer-generated randomization program.

domain_judgments.rationale: The allocation sequence was computer generated and centrally implemented by telephone, providing adequate sequence generation and concealment, and baseline characteristics were well matched within each trial.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Randomisation to the selected conventional approach or laparoscopic hysterectomy alternative was made by telephone access to a computer-generated randomisation programme held at the Northern and Yorkshire Clinical Trials Research Unit.

domain_judgments.rationale: Although blinding was infeasible and some preoperative treatment changes occurred, conversions were documented, the primary analysis followed intention-to-treat, and sensitivity and per-protocol analyses gave results in the same direction.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The primary analysis was by intention to treat. We also performed a secondary analysis of the primary end point, according to the procedure that was started (per protocol analysis).

domain_judgments.rationale: For the primary outcome, only 34 of 1380 randomized participants did not undergo surgery, and explicit worst-case sensitivity analyses addressed their missing complication outcomes without materially changing the direction of findings.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: We undertook sensitivity analyses for the 34 patients who did not actually have an operation.

domain_judgments.rationale: The primary outcome used prespecified objective clinical complication criteria applied across groups, with independent clinical review for potentially judgment-dependent anaesthetic complications, making differential ascertainment unlikely despite lack of blinding.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: An independent clinical reviewer differentiated between major and minor anaesthetic problems.

domain_judgments.rationale: The primary endpoint and analysis methods were clearly prespecified in the report, but no prospective protocol, registry entry, or prespecified statistical analysis plan is provided to exclude selective choice among analyses or outcome definitions.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The primary end point of the trials was the occurrence of at least one major complication (box 1).

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is judged some concerns, driven by the absence of an accessible prospective protocol or analysis plan needed to rule out selective reporting. Randomization and concealment were robust, the primary analysis was intention-to-treat, primary-outcome missingness was small and examined in sensitivity analyses, and major complications were defined objectively.

paper_title: A prospective randomized comparison of vaginal hysterectomy, laparoscopically assisted vaginal hysterectomy, and total laparoscopic hysterectomy in women with benign uterine disease
design_rationale: The abstract explicitly describes a prospective randomized study in which 125 women were randomly assigned to VH, LAVH, or TLH.

domain_judgments.rationale: Random assignment is stated, but the abstract provides no information on sequence generation, allocation concealment, or baseline comparability.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: A total of 125 women indicated to undergo hysterectomy for benign uterine disease were randomly assigned to three different groups (40 VH, 44 LAVH, and 41 TLH).

domain_judgments.rationale: Conversions occurred in every group, but the abstract does not report whether these deviations were intervention-related or whether participants were analyzed according to randomized assignment.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Conversions to another hysterectomy method occurred in all three groups, most of these conversions were to LAVH.

domain_judgments.rationale: The abstract reports enrollment and group sizes but does not state the number included in each outcome analysis or describe missing outcome data and exclusions.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: A total of 125 women indicated to undergo hysterectomy for benign uterine disease were randomly assigned to three different groups (40 VH, 44 LAVH, and 41 TLH).

domain_judgments.rationale: The outcomes are generally appropriate clinical measures, but the abstract does not describe standardized measurement procedures or blinded assessment, and some outcomes such as complications and analgesic use could be influenced by knowledge of surgical assignment.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Outcome measures, including operating time, blood loss, rate of complications, inflammatory response, febrile morbidity, consumption of analgesics, and length of hospital stay, were assessed and compared between groups.

domain_judgments.rationale: No prespecified protocol, registration, or analysis plan is reported, while numerous outcomes and possible analyses create scope for selective reporting.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Outcome measures, including operating time, blood loss, rate of complications, inflammatory response, febrile morbidity, consumption of analgesics, and length of hospital stay, were assessed and compared between groups.

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is judged as some concerns. The abstract confirms random assignment, but does not report sequence generation or concealment, handling of treatment conversions, completeness of outcome data, blinded or standardized outcome assessment, or prespecified outcome analyses.

domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Ninety women... were randomised into three groups for either technique of hysterectomy, thirty in each group, by the same surgeon.

domain_judgments.rationale: The abstract does not report attrition, exclusions after randomization, or the number of participants included in each outcome analysis, so completeness of outcome data cannot be established.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Ninety women with benign disease of uterus... were randomised into three groups... thirty in each group.

domain_judgments.rationale: Operative measures such as time and blood loss are generally appropriate, but blinding of outcome assessment is not reported and subjective outcomes including pain, satisfaction, and surgical difficulty could have been influenced by knowledge of treatment assignment.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: For each patient, intra-operative parameters including total duration of surgery, blood loss, surgical difficulty and intra-operative complications were recorded. domain_judgments.evidence_quote: No intraoperative complications or conversion to laparotomy occurred.

domain_judgments.evidence_quote: One hundred and eight women requiring hysterectomy for enlarged myomatous uterus were randomly allocated into three treatment arms: TLH (n = 36); LAVH (n = 36); VH (n = 36).

paper_title: Vaginal hysterectomy versus laparoscopically assisted vaginal hysterectomy for large uteri between 280 and 700 g: a randomized controlled trial
design_rationale: The Methods explicitly describe the study as a prospective randomized controlled trial in which 50 patients were divided into two intervention groups.

domain_judgments.rationale: Although the trial is described as randomized and baseline characteristics were reportedly similar, the abstract does not describe sequence generation or allocation concealment.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Prospective randomized controlled trial done at Ain Shams University Maternity Hospital, where 50 patients were recruited and divided into two equal groups (each 25 patients).

domain_judgments.rationale: The surgical procedures necessarily made blinding of clinicians impractical, and the available text does not report protocol deviations, crossover, or whether participants were analyzed according to randomized assignment.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: First group underwent vaginal hysterectomy, and the second underwent laparoscopically assisted vaginal hysterectomy.

domain_judgments.rationale: The abstract reports two groups of 25 but does not provide participant flow or explicitly confirm that outcome data were available for every randomized patient.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: 50 patients were recruited and divided into two equal groups (each 25 patients).

domain_judgments.rationale: The reported surgical and cost outcomes are generally appropriate and appear measured across both groups, but assessor blinding and standardized measurement procedures—particularly for estimated blood loss and complications—are not described.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: As for surgical outcomes, estimated intraoperative blood loss (P = 0.90), operative time (P = 0.48), preoperative hemoglobin (P = 0.09), postoperative hemoglobin (P = 0.42), and operative complications (P = 1.0) did not differ between the two groups.

domain_judgments.rationale: Prospective trial registration reduces concern, but the supplied text does not provide the registered protocol or prespecified analysis plan needed to exclude selective choice among multiple outcomes or analyses.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The study was registered in ClinicalTrials.gov (Id NCT02826304) prior to initiation.

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is judged as some concerns. The study is explicitly randomized and prospectively registered, but the available report lacks details on sequence generation and concealment, participant flow and analysis by assignment, outcome-assessment safeguards, and prespecified analyses.

domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Procedures were successfully performed for all the patients in both groups... No conversion to laparotomy was necessary.

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcome results appear available for all 80 randomized patients, with successful procedures in both groups and no reported losses or exclusions after randomization.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The enrollment was closed when 80 patients were included, and 40 patients were allocated to each group... Procedures were successfully performed for all the patients in both groups.

domain_judgments.rationale: The primary outcome of discharge time was objectively measured using prespecified, standardized criteria applied across groups, and outcome assessors were reported to be blinded to assignment.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The patients were discharged from the hospital when they were tolerant of a normal diet, able to dress themselves, fully mobile, apyrexial, and not requiring analgesics... Those assessing the outcomes were blinded to the group assignments.

domain_judgments.rationale: The primary and secondary outcomes are identified in the article, but no trial registration, protocol, or prespecified statistical analysis plan is reported, and several analyses and outcome categorizations could permit selective reporting.
